quarterly_data.quarter: Kyocera results briefing Q&A: Speech and Q&A for Q1 FY2027 (07-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: President Sakushima (Q1 of fiscal 2027, three months ended June 30, 2026): sales revenue rose 9.9% year on year to JPY525.4 billion and operating profit 164.7% to JPY49.1 billion; profit before income taxes JPY74.9 billion (+68.1%) and profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY60.6 billion (+63.1%), both sales and profit record highs for a first quarter. Core Components sales JPY178.1 billion with business profit JPY23.8 billion (13.4% margin), driven by fine ceramic components for semiconductor processing equipment and semiconductor packages for AI data centers; Electronic Components sales JPY103.6 billion with business profit JPY8.8 billion (8.5%), on small-sized high-capacitance MLCCs and tantalum capacitors for AI data centers and including about JPY3 billion from the sale of real estate; Solutions sales JPY247.6 billion with business profit JPY30.3 billion, down in sales after the transfer of a US subsidiary of the Industrial Tools Unit. The weaker yen (average JPY159 to the US dollar and JPY185 to the euro) added approximately JPY35 billion to sales revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 FY2027 sales revenue JPY525.4 billion (+9.9%); operating profit JPY49.1 billion (+164.7%); Core Components sales JPY178.1 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Kyocera results briefing Q&A: Speech and Q&A for Q1 FY2027 (07-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Revised forecast for fiscal 2027 (year ending March 31, 2027), raised from April: sales revenue up JPY140 billion to JPY2.08 trillion, business profit up JPY30 billion to JPY160 billion, profit before income taxes JPY200 billion and profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY160 billion, assuming JPY155 to the US dollar and JPY180 to the euro; sales forecasts raised by JPY62 billion for Core Components, JPY51 billion for Electronic Components and JPY32 billion for Solutions, mainly on market expansion of products for AI data centers and exchange rates. Capex, depreciation and R&D forecasts are unchanged. Management still expects rising raw material prices and geopolitical risks to show from Q2 onward; President Sakushima said the 1Q upside came from demand arriving earlier than planned, figures for Q2 onward are kept as originally projected, and 1H and 2H are expected at roughly the same level. The ROE forecast was raised to 4.9%, aiming to reach the 5% or higher target for the year ending March 31, 2028 one year ahead of schedule.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 forecast: sales revenue JPY2.08 trillion; business profit JPY160 billion; profit before income taxes JPY200 billion; ROE 4.9%

quarterly_data.quarter: Kyocera results briefing Q&A: Speech and Q&A for Q1 FY2027 (07-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Components investment plan (President Sakushima): about JPY650 billion over the six years from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2031, focused on advanced semiconductors and AI-related areas; investment rises to about JPY150 billion in fiscal 2027 as the Nagasaki Isahaya Plant is scheduled for completion that year, then continues at about JPY100 billion a year from fiscal 2028, with the goal of raising sales of the advanced semiconductor and AI-related businesses to 2.8 times the fiscal 2026 level.
quarterly_data.figure: About JPY650 billion over fiscal 2026-2031; about JPY150 billion in fiscal 2027; about JPY100 billion a year from fiscal 2028; AI-related sales goal 2.8 times fiscal 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Kyocera results briefing Q&A: Speech and Q&A for Q1 FY2027 (07-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: President Sakushima on supply and demand: demand for ceramic components for semiconductor processing equipment, expected to stay sluggish until around the end of last year, turned sharply at the start of this calendar year and showed up as actual orders from fiscal 2027; the upward revision came from higher demand from existing customers rather than share gains. Major customers have provided a solid annual demand outlook, so Kyocera will consider expanding its production workforce and bringing forward capacity investment. Ceramic packages for optical communications: after capacity was scaled back when telecom-infrastructure demand fell, demand has risen again with optical links between data centers; there is currently a shortfall in production capacity and the company is ramping up and investing to expand it. Organic packages: availability of glass core material is currently the bottleneck, but yield and productivity improvements are raising shipments and the company can now meet rising demand from existing customers. Tantalum capacitors: demand could not be fully met because of capacity constraints, but productivity gains at KAVX's Thai plant have raised output slightly. Customers' requested quantities keep increasing in direct discussions, and he believes strong demand will continue, particularly for the current fiscal year.

quarterly_data.quarter: Kyocera results briefing Q&A: Speech and Q&A for Q1 FY2027 (07-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: MLCCs for AI servers and semiconductors (President Sakushima): against rapidly rising data-center and semiconductor demand, Kyocera is proceeding with signing long-term supply agreements for certain products, which he said let it gauge volumes, plan line balance and keep utilisation high, and it has begun arranging large-scale investments to expand capacity and raise new-product yields. MLCCs for AI data centers that use KAVX's proprietary terminal-shape technology have just entered mass production; MLCCs for telecommunications applications still account for the majority, and the company intends to raise the AI data center share and plans to repurpose KAVX production lines for the specific requirements it is receiving. He said there are still challenges in delivering stable quantities with consistent quality of cutting-edge products, and that the Electronic Components margin was flat quarter on quarter because crystal devices and connectors are weak while MLCC and tantalum margins rose.

quarterly_data.quarter: Kyocera results briefing Q&A: Speech and Q&A for Q1 FY2027 (07-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Solutions Business (President Sakushima): the Industrial Tools Unit saw last-minute demand in 1Q ahead of price increases passed on for sharply higher raw material prices, and a backlash is expected from 2Q; the Communications Unit is asking customers to accept device price increases because of memory prices and shipped early in 1Q at customers' request, so 2Q onward is slightly below the original projection with the full year roughly in line with the initial plan; the Document Solutions Unit's sales in Europe, its main market, are recovering to usual levels after last year's slowdown.
